questions.question: The Indian telecom sector was liberalised under which year’s Telecom Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian telecom sector was liberalized under the **National Telecom Policy of 1994**.
 
• The policy introduced **private sector participation** in providing telecom services, which was earlier monopolized by the government.
 
• It aimed to **increase tele-density** and improve the quality of services by allowing private players to operate in the telecom space.
 
• The 1994 policy laid the groundwork for further liberalization and reforms, including the entry of private companies in the telecom sector.
 
• This reform was a major step towards **modernizing India's telecom infrastructure** and ensuring widespread connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI):** Established in 1997, TRAI is responsible for regulating telecom services, including tariffs and ensuring fair competition.
 
• **Subsequent Policies:** The 1999 New Telecom Policy (NTP) further liberalized the sector and introduced revenue-sharing models instead of fixed license fees.
 
• **Telecom Revolution:** The liberalization and reforms of the 1990s paved the way for the telecom revolution in India, with rapid growth in mobile phone penetration and internet services.
 
• **FDI in Telecom:** The sector has also attracted significant foreign direct investment (FDI), with the government allowing up to 100% FDI in certain areas.
 
• **Impact:** Today, India is one of the largest telecom markets globally, with billions of subscribers and a robust digital infrastructure.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the vertical planetary mixer developed by ISRO in Feb 2025?

options.text: To develop new materials for spacecraft
To create advanced propulsion systems for deep space missions
To enhance the efficiency and safety of solid rocket motor manufacturing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To enhance the efficiency and safety of solid rocket motor manufacturing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **vertical planetary mixer** developed by ISRO in **February 2025** is designed to **enhance the efficiency and safety** in the production of solid rocket motors.
 
• This technology supports precise mixing of propellant ingredients, ensuring consistent quality and composition for **better performance of rockets**.
 
• Solid rocket motors are critical components in many launch vehicles, including those used for satellite deployment and interplanetary missions.
 
• The mixer integrates advanced mechanical design and automation features to **reduce human intervention**, minimizing risks associated with hazardous materials.
 
• ISRO has been focusing on innovations to streamline the manufacturing process of solid propulsion systems, which are vital for India’s space missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solid Rocket Motors:**

 
 
• Solid rocket motors use a solid propellant mixture that is ignited to produce thrust.
 
• They are simpler and more reliable compared to liquid propulsion systems but require meticulous manufacturing processes for consistent results.
 
• Propellant mixtures generally include oxidizers, fuel, and binders.
 
 
 
• **Planetary Mixers:**
 
 
• Planetary mixers are specialized machines designed for mixing viscous materials uniformly.
 
• They are widely used in industries like food, chemical, and aerospace manufacturing.
 
• The "vertical" design enhances efficiency by reducing material settling and ensuring thorough mixing.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Advancements in Propulsion:**
 
 
• ISRO has developed several propulsion technologies, including cryogenic engines and solid rocket boosters.
 
• Solid propulsion systems are used in the PSLV and GSLV series for launching satellites into orbit.
 
• Continuous advancements aim to improve reliability, safety, and cost-effectiveness.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations in Propellant Manufacturing:**
 
 
• Propellant manufacturing involves handling hazardous chemicals and explosive materials.
 
• Automation and specialized equipment like vertical planetary mixers reduce the risks associated with human errors.
 
• Safety protocols and advanced designs are integral to ensuring worker safety and environmental protection.

questions.question: What is India's Human Development Index (HDI) value in the 2025 Human Development Index Report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.685**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Human Development Index (HDI) value for 2025 is projected to be **0.685**, as per the Human Development Index Report.
 
• The HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: **health, education, and standard of living**.
 
• India's HDI has been steadily improving due to consistent progress in **life expectancy, literacy rates, and per capita income**.
 
• India is classified as a country with **medium human development**, given its HDI value falls between 0.550 and 0.699.
 
• Despite improvements, India continues to face challenges such as **inequality, regional disparities, and low gender equality**, which impact its overall HDI ranking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**

 
 
• HDI is published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its Human Development Report.
 
• The index focuses on three dimensions: **health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (GNI per capita).**
 
• It ranges from 0 to 1, where a higher value indicates better human development outcomes.
 
 
 
• **India's HDI Trends**
 
 
• India's HDI value has seen consistent growth over the last few decades due to government initiatives in health, education, and poverty alleviation.
 
• For instance, India's HDI value was **0.645 in 2019**, and it has shown an upward trend despite challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)**
 
 
• IHDI accounts for inequality in the distribution of each dimension of HDI.
 
• India's IHDI value is typically lower than its HDI value, highlighting inequality in education, health, and income.
 
 
 
• **Global HDI Context**
 
 
• In the latest Human Development Report, countries like **Norway, Ireland, and Switzerland** rank highest in HDI.
 
• India's HDI ranking is typically around the **130-140 range**, reflecting its medium level of human development compared to global peers.

questions.question: In the Gender Inequality Index (GII) 2022, what rank did India achieve among 193 countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**108**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India ranked **108** out of **193 countries** in the Gender Inequality Index (GII) 2022, as reported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The Gender Inequality Index measures disparities in gender-based achievements across **health, empowerment, and labor market participation**.
 
• India's performance in the index reflects challenges in areas such as **women’s participation in politics, workforce involvement, and reproductive health**.
 
• The GII is part of the Human Development Report published by the **UNDP**, which serves as a global benchmark for assessing gender equality.
 
• India's ranking indicates ongoing efforts and room for improvement in addressing gender disparities in various sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gender Inequality Index (GII):**

 
 
• The GII was introduced in the **Human Development Report 2010** to reflect the loss in human development due to inequality between genders.
 
• It focuses on three dimensions: **reproductive health, empowerment, and labor market participation**.
 
• Empowerment is measured through women’s participation in decision-making, including their presence in parliamentary roles and education levels.
 
 
 
• **India’s Progress:**
 
 
• India has made improvements in areas such as maternal health and education for women, but challenges remain in **women’s representation in politics and workforce**.
 
• Increasing focus on government initiatives like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** aims to address gender disparities.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends:**
 
 
• Countries with higher development indices generally score better on gender equality due to **inclusive policies and social reforms**.
 
• Nordic countries such as Iceland and Norway consistently rank among the top performers in the GII.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminologies:**
 
 
• **Reproductive Health:** Includes indicators like maternal mortality and adolescent birth rates.
 
• **Empowerment:** Refers to access to education and political representation.
 
• **Labor Market Participation:** Measures female participation in the workforce relative to men.

questions.question: As of April 2025, what percentage of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA) has been finalised, bringing both the nations closer to concluding the deal?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of April 2025, **90% of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA)** has been finalized, marking significant progress in negotiations.
 
• The India-UK FTA is aimed at enhancing trade relations by reducing tariffs, increasing market access, and fostering economic cooperation.
 
• Both nations are working towards concluding the deal to boost bilateral trade, which currently stands at over **£34 billion annually**.
 
• The agreement covers key sectors such as technology, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, and financial services.
 
• The finalization of the agreement is expected to strengthen ties and contribute to mutual economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Trade Agreement (FTA):**

 
 
• FTA is a pact between two or more nations to reduce or eliminate trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas.
 
• It aims to promote free flow of goods and services between member countries.
 
 
 
• **India's Trade Policy:**
 
 
• India actively pursues FTAs to enhance its global trade footprint and attract foreign investments.
 
• Major FTAs include agreements with ASEAN, Japan, South Korea, and the UAE.
 
 
 
• **UK's Post-Brexit Trade Strategy:**
 
 
• After exiting the EU, the UK has focused on establishing FTAs with countries worldwide, including India.
 
• This strategy is designed to mitigate economic impacts post-Brexit and expand trade opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of FTA:**
 
 
• FTAs can lead to increased exports, job creation, and lower costs for consumers due to reduced tariffs.
 
• They also foster innovation and global competitiveness among domestic industries.

questions.question: Which country became the first in Latin America to exit China's Belt and Road Initiative in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panama**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Panama became the first Latin American country to exit China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in 2025, signaling a shift in its geopolitical alliances.
 
• The Belt and Road Initiative, launched by China in 2013, is a global infrastructure development strategy aimed at increasing economic and trade connectivity.
 
• Panama had initially joined the BRI in 2017, under the presidency of Juan Carlos Varela, to boost trade and investment ties with China.
 
• Panama's decision to exit the BRI aligns with its efforts to diversify its trade partnerships and reduce dependence on China amid global geopolitical tensions.
 
• The withdrawal has sparked discussions on the long-term sustainability and geopolitical implications of the BRI in Latin America.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI):**

 
 
• The BRI is a global development strategy initiated by China to invest in infrastructure projects such as roads, railways, and ports in over 140 countries.
 
• It aims to improve trade routes and foster economic integration across Asia, Europe, Africa, and Latin America.
 
 
 
• **Panama's Geopolitical Position:**
 
 
• Panama holds a strategic location due to the Panama Canal, a critical waterway connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
 
• Its geopolitical decisions have significant implications for global trade and security dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Impact of BRI Withdrawal:**
 
 
• Panama's exit from the BRI may influence other Latin American countries to reconsider their participation in the initiative.
 
• It highlights concerns over debt sustainability and the strategic autonomy of participating nations.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Partnerships:**
 
 
• Panama is exploring stronger economic ties with the United States and European Union to balance its trade relations.
 
• These partnerships aim to provide an alternative to Chinese investments and infrastructure projects.

questions.question: How many cities were initially included under the Smart Cities Mission launched by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Government of India on **25 June 2015** under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
 
• Initially, **100 cities** were selected to be developed as part of the mission.
 
• The mission aims to improve urban infrastructure and provide better quality of life through **sustainable and inclusive development**.
 
• The cities were selected through a competitive process known as the **Smart Cities Challenge**.
 
• The total planned investment for the mission is estimated at **₹2.05 lakh crore**, covering projects like affordable housing, urban mobility, and IT connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission Objectives:**

 
 
• The mission focuses on **area-based development** such as retrofitting, redevelopment, and greenfield projects.
 
• It emphasizes **smart solutions** like smart meters, intelligent traffic management, and e-governance.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process:**
 
 
• The cities were selected through a **three-stage competition** involving state governments, urban local bodies, and central government evaluation.
 
• Only cities that meet specified criteria are granted funding under the mission.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• Each selected city sets up a **Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)** for implementation, with support from government and private partners.
 
• The SPV is responsible for planning, appraising, and executing projects under the mission.
 
 
 
• **Progress:**
 
 
• As of 2023, over 7,000 projects have been tendered, with many nearing completion across various cities.
 
• Key focus areas include **urban mobility, affordable housing, and green energy initiatives**.

questions.question: What is India’s renewable energy target by the year 2030 in terms of installed capacity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500 GW**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has set an ambitious target of achieving **500 GW of renewable energy installed capacity** by the year 2030.
 
• This target includes contributions from various renewable sources such as **solar, wind, hydropower, and biomass.**
 
• The initiative is part of India's commitment under the **Paris Agreement** to combat climate change and reduce carbon emissions.
 
• India aims to fulfill **50% of its energy requirements** from renewable sources by 2030.
 
• As of 2023, India has already achieved around **125 GW of renewable energy capacity**, showcasing significant progress toward the 2030 goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Solar Mission (NSM):**

 
 
• Launched in 2010, NSM is part of India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).
 
• It aims to establish India as a global leader in solar energy by achieving a target of **100 GW of solar capacity** by 2022.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• An international treaty adopted in 2015 to combat climate change.
 
• India pledged to reduce its carbon intensity by **33-35% by 2030** compared to 2005 levels.
 
• Renewable energy targets are a key component of India's commitment under this agreement.
 
 
 
• **International Solar Alliance (ISA):**
 
 
• Founded by India and France in 2015, ISA is a treaty-based intergovernmental organization.
 
• Its objective is to promote the use of solar energy globally and mobilize financial resources for its expansion.
 
 
 
• **Green Energy Corridor Project:**
 
 
• A government initiative to integrate renewable energy into India's power grid.
 
• The project involves setting up transmission networks to handle renewable energy efficiently.

questions.question: What milestone did Virat Kohli achieve in the 2025 IPL season (as of 15 April, 2025)?

options.text: Registering a combined total of 1000 fours and sixes in IPL history

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Registering a combined total of 1000 fours and sixes in IPL history**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Virat Kohli **became the first player in IPL history to achieve the milestone of **registering a combined total of 1000 fours and sixes** as of April 15, 2025.
 
• The milestone includes a career record of over **850 fours and 150 sixes**, showcasing his consistency and dominance as a batsman in the league.
 
• Kohli has been a part of the IPL since its inception in 2008 and has represented **Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB)** throughout his IPL career.
 
• This achievement underscores Kohli's role as one of the most prolific run-scorers in IPL history, further solidifying his legacy in T20 cricket.
 
• He has also been the **leading run-scorer in IPL history**, with over 7000 runs to his name as of 2025.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Premier League (IPL):**

 
 
• The IPL is a professional T20 cricket league in India, founded in 2008 by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
 
• It is one of the most popular and lucrative cricket leagues globally, featuring players from across the world.
 
• The league consists of **10 franchise teams** representing different cities in India (as of 2025).
 
• Notable records in the IPL include most runs, most wickets, and highest individual scores in a match.
 
 
 
• **Virat Kohli:**
 
 
• Virat Kohli is regarded as one of the greatest batsmen of all time, known for his consistency across all formats of cricket.
 
• He has represented India in all three formats and has captained the national team across various tournaments.
 
• Kohli holds several records, including being the fastest to 8000, 9000, 10000, 11000, and 12000 ODI runs.
 
• In IPL, he holds the record for the most runs scored in a single season (973 runs in 2016).
 
 
 
• **T20 Cricket:**
 
 
• T20 cricket is a shorter format of the game, with each team playing a maximum of 20 overs.
 
• It emphasizes aggressive batting, innovative bowling, and quick fielding to achieve results within a few hours.
 
• The format has gained immense popularity due to its fast-paced nature and entertainment value.
 
 
 
• **Milestones in IPL:**
 
 
• Several players have achieved unique milestones, including **Chris Gayle** (most sixes in IPL history) and **Lasith Malinga** (most wickets in IPL history).
 
• Milestones like 1000 fours and sixes reflect a player's ability to consistently score boundaries, a critical skill in T20 cricket.
 
• Such records highlight the evolution of cricket as a sport and the growing emphasis on strike rates and scoring efficiency.

questions.question: How much percentage of rural families rely on agriculture, livestock and Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFP) for their livelihoods according to the Annual Report 2024-25, published by Ministry of Rural Development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**90%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the **Annual Report 2024-25** published by the Ministry of Rural Development, around **90%** of rural families rely on agriculture, livestock, and Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFP) for their livelihoods.
 
• This data underscores the significant dependency of rural households on these sectors for both income generation and food security.
 
• **Non-Timber Forest Products** (NTFP) include resources like bamboo, honey, medicinal plants, and other forest-derived materials that are crucial for rural livelihoods.
 
• Livelihood diversification in rural areas is often centered around a combination of agriculture, livestock rearing, and forest-based activities.
 
• Such dependency also highlights the vulnerability of rural families to climate change, economic disruptions, and environmental degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agriculture in Rural India:**

 
 
• Agriculture is the primary source of livelihood for rural households, contributing significantly to India's GDP.
 
• Small and marginal farmers constitute the majority, with holdings of less than 2 hectares.
 
• Seasonal crops and monsoon dependence make rural agriculture vulnerable to climatic variations.
 
 
 
• **Livestock in Rural Livelihoods:**
 
 
• Livestock rearing provides supplementary income and acts as a risk mitigation strategy during crop failures.
 
• India is the largest producer of milk globally, with livestock being a key contributor to rural economies.
 
• Livestock products like milk, eggs, and meat are crucial for nutritional security in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFP):**
 
 
• NTFPs include bamboo, lac, resin, honey, medicinal plants, and other forest-based resources.
 
• These products are especially significant for tribal communities and forest-dwelling populations.
 
• NTFPs contribute to both sustenance and income generation, with many rural families relying on them for daily needs.
 
 
 
• **Challenges for Rural Livelihoods:**
 
 
• Climate change, deforestation, and over-exploitation of natural resources pose threats to sustainability.
 
• Lack of market access, infrastructure, and financial support hinders income growth for rural families.
 
• Government initiatives like MGNREGA and rural development schemes aim to address these challenges.

questions.question: What is the capital expenditure (CAPEX) allocated for Indian Railways in the financial year 2024-25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.62 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **capital expenditure (CAPEX) allocated for Indian Railways** in the financial year 2024-25 has been set at ₹2.62 lakh crore.
 
• This allocation marks a **significant increase** compared to previous years, underlining the government's focus on infrastructure development.
 
• It is the **highest-ever CAPEX allocation** for Indian Railways, aimed at modernizing and expanding railway infrastructure.
 
• The funds will be utilized for projects such as **track doubling, electrification, station redevelopment, and rolling stock acquisition**.
 
• Emphasis has also been placed on **high-speed rail projects** and improving passenger amenities across the railway network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Expenditure (CAPEX):**

 
 
• CAPEX refers to funds used by an organization or government to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets like infrastructure, buildings, or equipment.
 
• In the context of Indian Railways, it includes investments in projects like electrification, new lines, and station redevelopment.
 
 
 
• **Indian Railways Modernization:**
 
 
• The modernization plan includes electrification of routes, the introduction of semi-high-speed and high-speed trains, and enhanced safety measures.
 
• It also focuses on automation and the use of technology to improve operational efficiency.
 
 
 
• **High-Speed Rail Projects:**
 
 
• India's flagship high-speed rail project is the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor.
 
• Such projects are expected to reduce travel time and boost regional economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Green Initiatives:**
 
 
• Indian Railways aims to achieve **net-zero carbon emissions by 2030**, with a focus on renewable energy and electrification of rail routes.
 
• Large-scale solar and wind energy projects are being integrated into railway operations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Increased CAPEX:**
 
 
• Higher CAPEX in railways is expected to boost employment, regional connectivity, and economic growth.
 
• It is also likely to improve logistics efficiency, reducing costs for businesses and consumers.

questions.question: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 introduced which significant change to the composition of Waqf Boards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inclusion of non-Muslim members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** introduced a historic change by allowing the **inclusion of non-Muslim members** in Waqf Boards.
 
• This amendment aims to promote **inclusivity and transparency** in the functioning of Waqf Boards, which traditionally consisted only of Muslim members.
 
• Non-Muslim members are expected to contribute to **better accountability and broader representation** within Waqf Boards.
 
• The inclusion helps address concerns regarding the management of Waqf properties and ensures that they are administered in a manner that serves diverse communities.
 
• The amendment aligns with the government's efforts to modernize Waqf administration and reduce instances of mismanagement of Waqf properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waqf:**

 
 
• A Waqf is a **permanent dedication of movable or immovable property by a Muslim for religious, pious, or charitable purposes**.
 
• Once declared as Waqf, the property cannot be sold, transferred, or inherited.
 
• Waqfs are governed under the **Waqf Act, 1995**, which was later amended in subsequent years.
 
 
 
• **Role of Waqf Boards:**
 
 
• Waqf Boards are responsible for the administration and management of Waqf properties within their jurisdiction.
 
• They ensure that properties are used for the purposes intended, such as funding schools, mosques, hospitals, or other social welfare activities.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Waqf Property Management:**
 
 
• Instances of corruption, mismanagement, and illegal encroachments have plagued Waqf property administration.
 
• Reforms such as the inclusion of non-Muslim members aim to bring greater accountability and efficiency to the system.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to Waqf Legislation:**
 
 
• Recent amendments have focused on **digitization of records**, streamlining audits, and empowering boards to take strict actions against encroachments.
 
• The inclusion of non-Muslim members is a progressive step towards making Waqf Boards more diverse and democratic.

questions.question: In April 2025, Chief Justice Sanjiv Khanna named _____ as his successor, who will be the _____ upon appointment

options.text: Justice B R Gavai; 53rd Chief Justice of India
Justice B R Gavai; 52ⁿd Chief Justice of India
Justice Hima Kohli; 53rd Chief Justice of India
Justice Surya Kant; 51st Chief Justice of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice B R Gavai; 52nd Chief Justice of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Justice Sanjiv Khanna, the 51st Chief Justice of India**, retired in May 2025, as per the standard retirement age of 65 for Supreme Court judges.
 
• **Justice B R Gavai** has been named as his successor, making him the **52nd Chief Justice of India** upon appointment.
 
• Justice B R Gavai is known for his significant contributions to the judiciary and has been part of several landmark judgments during his tenure in the Supreme Court.
 
• He will be the second Chief Justice of India from the Scheduled Caste community, following Justice K G Balakrishnan, who served as the 37th CJI.
 
• The appointment of the Chief Justice of India is made by the President of India based on seniority among the Supreme Court judges and recommendations from the outgoing CJI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI):**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary system and the Supreme Court, the highest constitutional court in India.
 
• The CJI plays a vital role in upholding the Constitution, interpreting laws, and maintaining checks and balances between the three branches of government.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for the CJI:**
 
 
• Must be a citizen of India.
 
• Must have served as a judge in a High Court for at least five years or as an advocate in a High Court for at least ten years, or be a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• The President of India appoints the CJI based on seniority among the judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• The outgoing CJI recommends their successor in consultation with other senior judges of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Retirement Age:**
 
 
• Supreme Court judges, including the CJI, retire at the age of 65.
 
• High Court judges, by comparison, retire at the age of 62.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Justice H J Kania was the first Chief Justice of India, serving from 1950 to 1951.
 
• Justice Fathima Beevi was the first woman to be appointed as a Supreme Court judge in India, paving the way for greater representation in the judiciary.

questions.question: Which country assumed the presidency of BRICS in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brazil **assumed the **presidency of BRICS **in **January 2025**, continuing the annual rotation of leadership among member countries.
 
• BRICS is an acronym for five major emerging economies:** Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.
 
• The presidency of BRICS rotates annually in alphabetical order among its members.
 
• As the BRICS president, Brazil will oversee hosting summits, coordinating initiatives, and aligning efforts for economic cooperation among member countries in 2025.
 
• The BRICS presidency allows member countries to shape agendas focusing on global economic challenges and sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS Overview**

 
 
• BRICS was established in **2006**, **initially consisting of Brazil, Russia, India, and China, with South Africa joining in 2010**.
 
• The organization focuses on fostering cooperation in areas such as trade, finance, infrastructure, and sustainable development.
 
• The BRICS nations collectively represent approximately** 40% of the global population and over 20% of the world’s GDP**.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Presidency**
 
 
• The presidency rotates alphabetically among member countries every year.
 
• Responsibilities include hosting the annual BRICS summit, coordinating agendas, and spearheading collaborative efforts.
 
• South Africa held the presidency in 2023, followed by Russia in 2024, and Brazil in 2025.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by BRICS**
 
 
• **New Development Bank** (NDB): Established in **2014 **to fund infrastructure and sustainable development projects.
 
• Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA): A framework to provide financial support during global economic crises.
 
• BRICS Business Council: Promotes business collaboration among member nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of BRICS**
 
 
• BRICS plays a significant role in advocating for reforms in global financial institutions like the IMF and World Bank.
 
• It emphasizes addressing global challenges such as **climate change, poverty, and inequality**.
 
• The group seeks to create a multipolar world order, reducing reliance on Western-dominated institutions.
